title: Making an open box from a square sheet
body: A school's craft club makes open-topped storage boxes from square sheets of cardboard, each of side 18 cm. From each corner of a sheet, a square of side x cm is cut out, and the four flaps that remain are folded up to form the sides of an open box. The club wants to choose x so that the box holds as much as possible. Clearly x must be positive, and it must be less than 9 cm, since otherwise nothing would be left to form the base. The members decide to write the volume of the box as a function of x and use derivatives to find the value of x that gives the greatest volume, checking their answer with the second derivative test.
